## What Replaces DRS in the 2026 Regulations

DRS (Drag Reduction System) is replaced by a **fully active aerodynamics system** — commonly referred to as **""Active Aero""** — in the 2026 regulations. This is a fundamental shift from the single-element rear-wing flap of the current era to a **dual-element system** that adjusts **both the front and rear wings**.
### The Two Modes
The system operates in two distinct configurations, known colloquially as **X-Mode** and **Z-Mode**:
### Key Technical Details (from the 2026 Technical Regulations)
- **Front Wing Rotation System** (Article **C3.10.10**): The front wing profiles can rotate between two fixed positions.
- **Rear Wing Rotation System** (Article **C3.11.6**): The RW Flap adjusts incidence between Corner Mode and Straight-Line Mode.
- **Transition time**: Maximum of **400ms** between the two fixed positions.
- **Single actuator** per system (electrical or fluidic), with position sensors linked to the FIA Standard ECU.
- **Deployment states** (Sporting Regulations, Article **B7.1.1**):
- **Deactivated** = both front and rear wings in Corner Mode (high incidence).
- **Partially activated** = front wing in Straight-Line Mode, rear wing in Corner Mode.
- **Fully activated** = both front and rear wings in Straight-Line Mode (low incidence).
### Activation Rules (Sporting Regulations, Article B7.1.3)
- Activation is only permitted when the car is **stationary** or within designated **Activation Zones**.
- The driver is notified via control electronics when the system is enabled.
- The system is **deactivated automatically** the first time the driver applies the brakes after activation.
- Under Safety Car conditions, activation is prohibited until the car crosses the line after the SC returns to the pits.
### Key Difference vs. DRS

Unlike DRS — which was a **single rear-wing flap** that opened only when within 1 second of the car ahead — the 2026 Active Aero system is a **driver-commanded, dual-wing system** that can be used more freely (subject to activation zones), and it works in concert with the new **manual override energy deployment** (MOU) system to manage the car's power delivery. The system is designed to work with the new 50/50 power unit split (roughly 50% ICE / 50% electrical) to balance drag reduction with the car's energy management.

## Override Mode (Overtake Mode) Deactivation Conditions — 2026 Regulations

Based on **Article B7.2.3** of the 2026 Sporting Regulations, Override Mode is deactivated under the following conditions during a **TTCS** (Track Time Competition Session — i.e., Qualifying and Race):
### 1. Gap-Based Deactivation (Article B7.2.3.c.ii)

> **Override Mode will be deactivated when the driver crosses the Activation Line, whilst Override Mode is activated, when their Car was greater than the Detection Gap behind another Car at the Detection Line.**

In plain terms: if a driver had Override Mode active (because they were within the Detection Gap at the Detection Line), but by the time they reach the **Activation Line** the gap to the car ahead has grown beyond the Detection Gap, the system is automatically deactivated.
### 2. Safety Car Deployment (Article B7.2.3.c.iii)
> **Override Mode may not be used by the driver from the time at which the safety car is deployed until they have crossed the Activation Line after the safety car has returned to the Pit Lane.**

This is reinforced by **Article B7.2.2.b**, which states the entire Override Mode **system** is disabled when the Safety Car is deployed, and only re-enabled when each car crosses the Line after the SC returns to the pit lane.
### 3. Race Director Discretion (Article B7.2.2.c)
The Race Director may, at their **absolute discretion**, disable the Override Mode system — partially or entirely — for safety reasons, including:
- **Low grip or poor visibility conditions** (Article B7.2.2.c.i) — the RD may disable all such systems until conditions improve.
### 4. System Disabling Prior to TTCS (Article B7.2.2.a)
The Override Mode system is **disabled prior to the start of any TTCS** and only enabled when the leader crosses the Detection Line for the first time during the session.
### Summary Table

- **2025:** The fuel mass flow measured by the FFM was checked directly against the mass-flow limits.

The **physical hardware requirements remain largely consistent** — both years mandate:

- Constant fuel pressures above 90 kg/h
